F

F · landing descent

How fast can the landing descent go before the vortex-ring state?

Descent rate used (lowest cap)

1.76 m/s

F_descent.v_cap_ms[0]

binding: vortex_ring_state

Source of kappa

Johnson, NASA/TP-2005-213477, Yeates test data: observable vortex ring state from Vz/vh = -0.23 near zero forward speed (the most conservative onset reported; Drees roughness -0.62 to -1.53, inflow instability -0.5 to -1.5). Read from a summary of the report: confirm against the PDF before quoting [documented]

F_descent.kappa_source[0]

Descent rate against time to go

The commanded descent rate along the profile, one line per scenario: the vortex-ring limit (kappa x the hover induced velocity) until the last few metres, then a ramp to the final rate. The time counts down to touchdown, so the flight reads right to left.

S-01, 0 mS-02, 5000 mS-03, 5000 mS-05, 500 mS-06, 5000 m

Energy to go against time to go

Hover energy still to be spent, one line per scenario: the hover power times the time to go, so each line is straight and its slope is the scenario's hover power.

S-01, 0 mS-02, 5000 mS-03, 5000 mS-05, 500 mS-06, 5000 m

not in this run: the margin to the vortex-ring onset against time (not written)

Register against recommended settings

E repeated at the AIRSPEED_MIN and TKOFF_THR_MAX of the FT optimum (D re-run at that entry speed). The register case is the headline above. The last two columns are information only. e_fwd_kJ is E's forward transition: the quasi-steady wait to AIRSPEED_MIN plus the rotor fade of Q_TRANSITION_MS (the rotors fade from the throttle that carries the share of the weight the wing does not, E.fade_wing_share). ft_site_energy_kJ is the mean energy of FT's simulated transition (hover to the end of the fade) over the FT members nearest to that site in the same case, with its wait and fade parts and the member count; e_fwd_over_ft is E divided by it. The members of a group still differ in mass, ISA, headwind and SoC and in altitude by up to about 1 km, so the ratio is a like-for-like size check by site, not a validation.

Scenarios at the recommended settings

The scenarios of scenarios.yaml and the state each back transition starts from: the AIRBRAKE exit at AIRSPEED_MIN - 2, read as an equivalent airspeed, with the register's AIRSPEED_MIN (17 m/s) -> the recommended one (18 m/s). The columns with an arrow are register -> recommended (m/s, and degrees for the pitch): the entry true airspeed, the ground speed (the true airspeed less the headwind) and V/Vs, the true airspeed over the 1 g stall speed at the scenario's mass. The rotors start at 'idle' (C.rotor_start); the entry pitch is the trim pitch of the entry state when D.theta_fw0_deg is "trim".

What each analysis is

The analyses of this study, each with the question its chapter answers, what it writes and who reads it.

analysisasksgivesread by
AWhich entry speeds and decelerations keep the altitude, and what closes the window?The zero-altitude-loss feasibility map and the wing-angle window of the back transition.D's optional wing-angle cap
DWhich Q_TRANS_DECEL can the aircraft hold across the ensemble?The braking deceleration of 32 members from the AIRBRAKE exit and the recommended Q_TRANS_DECEL (a_rec).E (the planned deceleration), the settings sheet
FHow fast can the landing descent go before the vortex-ring state?The descent rate, time and hover energy of the last 30 m.E (the landing segment)
Q2Does the pusher give the forward acceleration the energy budget assumes?The pusher's acceleration up to AIRSPEED_MIN at TKOFF_THR_MAX, by altitude, mass and state of charge.E (the forward transition)
EDoes the energy budget close for the missions, with the reserves?Energy by segment, the reserve and the maximum range per site and mission against the 100 and 120 km requirements.the settings sheet (at the recommended settings)
FTWhich AIRSPEED_MIN, Q_TRANSITION_MS, TKOFF_THR_MAX and Q_TRAN_PIT_MAX make the forward transition without losing altitude or stalling?The searched settings, the register and the ArduPilot default side by side.E and Q2 re-run at the recommended settings, the settings sheet
CWhich four ArduPilot settings brake the aircraft from the AIRBRAKE exit at least energy?Q_BACKTRANS_MS, Q_A_ANGLE_MAX, Q_M_SPIN_MIN and Q_TRANS_DECEL, with the wing held to the margin, and the unconstrained search as a reference.the settings sheet
SensitivityWhich inputs move the headline outputs, and how well are they known?One-at-a-time swings and a Morris screening of the inputs, with each input's evidence grade.the reading of every other chapter

Energy against stopping distance

C: ensemble mean energy against the 95th-percentile distance, the optimum's ramp with q varied (each point is labelled with its q).

C: the optimum's ramp, q varied (hollow = a member is flagged)C register (q = 2)ArduPilot defaultC optimum

What this result rests on

alpha_s = 15.70 deg is a placeholder (the CFD shows no lift peak up to 15 deg), and the blend sharpness M = 70 1/rad is a numerical parameter that also sets C_L,max (1.444, at alpha_w = 13.43 deg): the size of the stall effect, and so the enforced result, is provisional. The rotor model has constant thrust and torque coefficients and no in-plane force (CT1, CT2, CQ1, CQ2, CH1 and k_mu are zero in the register): thrust does not change with airspeed and the rotors add no drag in forward flight.

The enforced configuration and the unconstrained reference

C twice: the wing held to the limit (the headline, written to the recommended settings) and not held (the model's lift falls from its peak to about a third within a few degrees, so the unconstrained optimum flies through the stall). The exposure columns are the worst member (the least wing share is the lowest over members); they are not penalised and not failure flags. Holding the wing below the limit costs 1.95 x the energy, 1.84 x the stopping distance and 1.94 x the stopping time of the unconstrained search; q is 1.11 against 2.07 m/s^2.

worst overshoot

worst end sink

The optimum relies on the overshoot and end-sink tolerances, which are PROPOSED, not on a measured limit. At the optimum the margins are 0.01 m and 1.75 m/s.

Search convergence

Best cost found by each seed; the spread of these is the T-12 check.

The seeds agree on J (spread 0.74%) but differ in the parameters (T_bt 1.09 to 5.73; theta_A 12.2 to 20; spin_min 0.0623 to 0.164): a flat ridge, not a single optimum.

Ensemble spread

One strip per metric, one dot per member; the ArduPilot default's members are the hollow grey dots below each strip.

member of the optimumflagged membermember of the ArduPilot defaulttolerance (PROPOSED)

No member of the optimum stops short of the target: the overshoot is positive in all 32 and ranges from 0.21 to 1.99 m. The end sink is at most 0.01 m/s. The stop target assumes the planned deceleration q from t = 0, while the pitch ramp over T_bt delays the braking, so the aircraft stops past it.

One-at-a-time sensitivity

One setting changes at a time. The change of the full J is dominated by the failure penalty, so the figure shows the failures and the smooth part of J apart; x marks a row where members fail (the tooltip has the expressions).

Time histories, S-07

Scenario S-07: altitude 1500 m, ISA offset +0 K, mass factor 1.00, SoC 0.80, headwind +0 m/s (1,500 m reference altitude (cruise reference), nominal). It lies inside the ensemble's range on every axis, at the edge of the range on headwind. The ArduPilot default loses 2.1 m of altitude here; its ensemble members lose at most 12.6 m. Optimum, register start and ArduPilot default through the wait, fade and done modes; the square on each airspeed curve is where that case's fade starts and the diamond where it is done (the vertical lines are the optimum's). The shaded band is the accepted altitude change.

End of the fade

Sink rate at the end of the fade against the projected minimum altitude change, one mark per member. A hollow mark is a flagged member. The loss limit (-10 m) is outside the range shown, which runs from -4.0 to -0.6 m.

Wing share at the hand-over

Share of the weight the wing carries when the pusher takes over (1 would be the whole weight), one strip per case and one dot per member. Within a case the hand-over speed is the setting, so the dots differ by the wing share only.

optimumregisterArduPilot defaultflagged member

Cost against Q_TRANSITION_MS

The best snapped cost found with Q_TRANSITION_MS fixed at each value (the other three searched, then snapped to ArduPilot's integers). The winner is marked; a hollow mark is a point whose snapped optimum still has flagged members, none here; a square is a point whose three-seed spread is above the T-12 limit, none here. Over the 15 grid points J runs from 0.759 (Q_TRANSITION_MS 17 s) to 0.878 (2 s), 15.7% above the lowest. At the register's Q_TRANSITION_MS (5 s) J is 0.839, +10.6% against the winner's. 5 of 15 points lie within the seed spread (0.39%) of the best: Q_TRANSITION_MS 15, 15.5, 16, 16.5, 17 s. The whole range is 0.4% of what re-tuning all four settings gains from the register start (J 31.30 to 0.759), so with the other three re-tuned the fade length is a second-order choice. Within 2 % of the best cost: Q_TRANSITION_MS 14, 15, 15.5, 16, 16.5, 17, 20 s.

Its cost J is 0.771, +0.012 against the optimum on the same ensemble (+4.2 seed spreads). It is reported, not recommended: the owner decides. Cost against AIRSPEED_MIN

The best cost found when AIRSPEED_MIN is fixed and the other three are searched, on a logarithmic axis (zero is not on it; it starts at the decade below the smallest cost) so neighbouring values can be told apart. A hollow mark has flagged members, named in its tooltip. Flag-free: 18, 19 m/s.

Final cost by seed

The cost each search seed ended at, with that seed's four settings in the tooltip. It is the end point of the seed, not its path: iteration data is not stored, so convergence itself is not shown.

One-at-a-time sensitivity

Absolute change of the cost J against the base evaluation (J = 0.7588) when one setting changes; a row shows its failing-member count. The axis is linear within the seed spread of zero and logarithmic beyond it, so the one large row does not flatten the others. The seed spread is 0.39% of J, 0.0030 in J. Apart from C_L,max, these inputs DO move J by more than that: TECS_TIME_CONST = 3.0 (-0.118, 0 failing), TECS_TIME_CONST = 8.0 (+0.186, 0 failing), TECS_INTEG_GAIN = 0.15 (+0.166, 0 failing), TECS_INTEG_GAIN = 0.6 (-0.149, 0 failing), rotor_lag_s = 0.0 (-0.005, 0 failing), rotor_lag_s = 0.5 (+0.005, 0 failing), z_vel_p = 2.5 (+0.020, 0 failing), z_vel_p = 10.0 (-0.012, 0 failing), TRIM_THROTTLE = 0.35 (+0.092, 0 failing), TRIM_THROTTLE = 0.55 (-0.043, 0 failing), tecs_start = cold (+0.055, 0 failing).

Notes

FT_params, FT_runs and FT_history evaluate the optimum, the register start and the ArduPilot default on the first 32 members of the Sobol sample and the 8 corners. The grid search, FT_grid, FT_sens and J_start use the first 16 members. The optimum is the best snapped point of FT_grid: whole m/s, whole degrees, whole percent and whole milliseconds, the values ArduPilot can take.

FT_robust and the optimum_robust row of FT_params are evaluated on the first 16 members, the ensemble of the sensitivities, and are reported only: no search, never the recommendation.

T-12 on the grid: 15 of 15 points have a three-seed spread within 1%. The winner (17 s) passes. Q_TRANSITION_MS within 2% of the best cost: 14, 15, 15.5, 16, 16.5, 17, 20 s.

Notes

Limitations

  • Back-transition: C. Forward transition: FT, when it is among the analyses; C does not cover it.
  • The forward transition in the energy budget is a quasi-steady estimate.
  • AIRSPEED_MIN: D, C and FT read it as an equivalent airspeed (D.entry_convention); Q2, which feeds E, reads it as an equivalent airspeed (Q2.feed_convention). Which one ArduPilot compares is open (O-02).
  • Input set is not release grade: 72 register entries are TBD: controller.altitude_hold.K_h, controller.altitude_hold.K_i, controller.altitude_hold.K_vh, controller.altitude_hold.i_max, controller.altitude_hold.v_dem_max, controller.ardupilot.AIRSPEED_MIN, ... (72 in all)

Needs CFD at 16-24 deg
